title.zh: 卷42 薛辯 寇贊 酈範 韓秀 堯暄
title.en: Volume 42: Xue Bian, Kou Zan, Li Fan, Han Xiu, Yao Xuan
title.raw: 卷42 薛辯 寇贊 酈範 韓秀 堯暄 Volume 42: Xue Bian, Kou Zan, Li Fan, Han Xiu, Yao Xuan

sentences.zh: 薛辯 寇讚 酈範 韓秀 堯暄

translations.literal: Xue Bian, Kou Zan, Li Fan, Han Xiu, Yao Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bian, Kou Zan, Li Fan, Han Xiu, and Yao Xuan.

sentences.zh: 薛辯，字允白。

translations.literal: Xue Bian, styled Yunbai.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bian, whose style name was Yunbai.

sentences.zh: 其先自蜀徙於河東之汾陰，因家焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors moved from Shu to Fenyin in Hedong and there established their household.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had moved from Shu to Fenyin in Hedong, where the family settled.

sentences.zh: 祖陶，與薛祖、薛落等分統部眾，故世號三薛。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tao, together with Xue Zu, Xue Luo, and others, each led a portion of the tribal following, and so they were called the Three Xue in their day.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tao, along with Xue Zu, Xue Luo, and others, had each commanded part of the tribal following, which is why their line was known as the Three Xue.

sentences.zh: 父強，復代領部落，而祖、落子孫微劣，強遂總攝三營。

translations.literal: His father Qiang again took charge of the tribe in succession, while the descendants of Zu and Luo had grown weak; Qiang then assumed overall command of all three camps.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiang succeeded again as head of the tribe; as the lines of Zu and Luo had declined, Qiang came to command all three camps together.

sentences.zh: 善綏撫，為民所歸，歷石虎、苻堅，常憑河自固。

translations.literal: He was skilled at soothing and winning people, and the populace rallied to him; through the reigns of Shi Hu and Fu Jian he often relied on the river as a natural defense.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at winning people through kindness, he drew the populace to his side; under Shi Hu and Fu Jian he habitually used the river as his stronghold.

sentences.zh: 仕姚興為鎮東將軍，入為尚書。

translations.literal: He served Yao Xing as General Who Pacifies the East and later entered court as Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served Yao Xing as General Who Pacifies the East and was later appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing at court.

sentences.zh: 強卒，辯復襲統其營，為興尚書郎、建威將軍、河北太守。

translations.literal: When Qiang died, Bian again inherited command of the camp and served Xing as Master of Writing Attendant, General Who Establishes Might, and Administrator of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiang's death, Bian inherited command of the camp and held the posts of Master of Writing Attendant, General Who Establishes Might, and Administrator of Hebei under Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 辯稍驕傲，頗失民心。

translations.literal: Bian gradually grew arrogant and lost much of the people's support.
translations.idiomatic: Bian gradually grew arrogant and lost much popular support.

sentences.zh: 劉裕平姚泓，辯舉營降裕，司馬德宗拜為寧朔將軍、平陽太守。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu pacified Yao Hong, Bian surrendered his camp to Yu, and Sima Dezong appointed him General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu conquered Yao Hong, Bian surrendered his camp to Liu Yu, and Emperor An of Jin appointed him General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 及裕失長安，辯來歸國，仍立功於河際，太宗授平西將軍、雍州刺史，賜爵汾陰侯。

translations.literal: When Yu lost Chang'an, Bian returned to our state, again rendering service along the river frontier; Emperor Taizong appointed him General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong Province and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yu lost Chang'an, Bian came back to Wei, where he again distinguished himself along the Yellow River frontier; Emperor Taizong made him General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong Province and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 泰常七年卒於位，年四十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taichang he died in office, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the seventh year of Taichang, at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 子謹，字法順，容貌魁偉，頗覽史傳。

translations.literal: His son Jin, styled Fashun, was imposing in stature and had read widely in historical writings.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin, styled Fashun, was imposing in build and had read widely in history.

sentences.zh: 劉裕擒泓，辟相府行參軍，隨裕渡江。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu captured Hong, he was summoned as Acting Army Aide of the Chancellor's household and accompanied Yu across the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu captured Yao Hong, Jin was recruited as acting army aide in the chancellor's household and crossed the Yangzi with Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 尋轉記室參軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to the post of Army Aide of the Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the post of records aide.

sentences.zh: 辯將歸國，密使報謹，遂自彭城來奔。

translations.literal: When Bian was about to return to the state, he secretly sent word to Jin, who then fled from Pengcheng to join him.
translations.idiomatic: As Bian prepared to return to Wei, he sent a secret message to Jin, who then fled from Pengcheng to join him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，授河東太守。

translations.literal: The court commended him and appointed him Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his conduct and appointed him Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 後襲爵平西將軍、汾陰侯。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the titles General Who Pacifies the West and Marquis of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited the rank of General Who Pacifies the West and the marquisate of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 謹所治與屈丐連接，結士抗敵，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: The territory Jin governed bordered that of Helian Qugai; he rallied local gentlemen to resist the enemy and won great authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: The region Jin governed bordered Helian Qugai's domain; by rallying local leaders to resist the enemy he won both authority and popular regard.

sentences.zh: 始光中，世祖詔奚斤討赫連昌，[1]敕謹領偏師前鋒鄉導。

translations.literal: In the Shiguang era, Emperor Taiwu ordered Xi Jin to attack Helian Chang and commanded Jin to lead a detached column as vanguard and local guide.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shiguang era, Emperor Taiwu ordered Xi Jin to campaign against Helian Chang and directed Jin to lead a detached force as vanguard and guide.

sentences.zh: 既克蒲坂，世祖以新舊之民并為一郡，謹仍為太守，遷秦州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: After Pucheng was taken, Emperor Taiwu merged the old and new populations into one commandery; Jin remained administrator, was promoted to Inspector of Qin Province, and kept his general's title.
translations.idiomatic: After the capture of Pucheng, Emperor Taiwu merged the old and new populations into a single commandery; Jin remained administrator, was promoted to Inspector of Qin Province, and retained his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 山胡白龍憑險作逆，世祖詔鎮南將軍奚眷與謹自太平北入，討平之。

translations.literal: The Mountain Hu leader Bai Long relied on rugged terrain to rebel; Emperor Taiwu ordered General Who Guards the South Xi Juan and Jin to enter from the north via Taiping and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mountain Hu leader Bai Long rebelled from mountain strongholds, Emperor Taiwu ordered General Who Guards the South Xi Juan and Jin to advance north from Taiping and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 除安西將軍、涪陵公，刺史如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Fuling, while retaining his inspectorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Fuling, while remaining inspector.

sentences.zh: 太延初，征吐沒骨，平之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiyan he campaigned against Tumog and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiyan era he campaigned against Tumog and subdued them.

sentences.zh: 謹自郡遷州，威惠兼備，風化大行。

translations.literal: When Jin moved from administering a commandery to governing a province, he combined authority with kindness, and civilizing influence flourished widely.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin rose from commandery administrator to provincial inspector, he combined stern authority with kindness, and civilizing influence spread throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 時兵荒之後，儒雅道息。

translations.literal: At that time, in the aftermath of war and devastation, the way of classical learning had fallen silent.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of war and devastation, classical learning had fallen into neglect.

sentences.zh: 謹命立庠，教以詩書，三農之暇，悉令受業，躬巡邑里，親加考試，於是河汾之地，儒道興焉。

translations.literal: Jin ordered schools established and taught the Odes and Documents; in the intervals of the three agricultural seasons he had all take instruction, personally toured the districts, and examined pupils himself, and thus along the He and Fen the Confucian way revived.
translations.idiomatic: Jin ordered schools established and had students taught the Odes and Documents; in the slack seasons of the farming year he required all to attend instruction, toured the districts in person to examine them, and thereby revived Confucian learning throughout the He and Fen region.

sentences.zh: 真君元年，徵還京師，除內都坐大官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenjun he was recalled to the capital and appointed Chief Director of the Inner Court Commissariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenjun he was recalled to the capital and appointed chief director of the inner court commissariat.

sentences.zh: 五年，為都將，從駕北討，以後期與中山王辰等斬於都南，時年四十四。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as chief commander and followed the emperor on the northern campaign; for arriving late he was executed south of the capital together with Prince Chen of Zhongshan and others, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he served as chief commander on the emperor's northern campaign; for falling behind schedule he was executed south of the capital together with Prince Chen of Zhongshan and others, at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 尋贈鎮西將軍、秦雍二州刺史，諡曰元公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was posthumously awarded the title General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qin and Yong provinces, with the posthumous name Duke Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qin and Yong provinces, with the posthumous title Duke Yuan.

sentences.zh: 長子初古拔，一曰車輅拔，本名洪祚，世祖賜名。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chuguba, also called Cheluba, was originally named Hongzuo and received his present name from Emperor Taiwu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Chuguba, also known as Cheluba, had originally been named Hongzuo before Emperor Taiwu bestowed his present name.

sentences.zh: 沉毅有器識，年始弱冠，司徒崔浩見而奇之。

translations.literal: Steadfast and resolute, with real capacity and insight, he had only just reached manhood when Minister of Education Cui Hao saw him and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast and perceptive, he had only just come of age when Minister of Education Cui Hao met him and was struck by his promise.

sentences.zh: 真君中，蓋吳擾動關右，薛永宗屯據河側，世祖親討之。

translations.literal: During Zhenjun, Gai Wu stirred unrest in the Guanxi region and Xue Yongzong held the riverbank; Emperor Taiwu campaigned against them in person.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenjun era, Gai Wu raised turmoil in Guanxi and Xue Yongzong held the riverbank; Emperor Taiwu led the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 乃詔拔糾合宗鄉，壁於河際，斷二寇往來之路。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Ba to rally the clans and townships, fortify positions along the river, and cut the route by which the two rebels communicated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ba to rally the clans and local communities, fortify positions along the river, and sever communications between the two rebel forces.

sentences.zh: 事平，除中散，賜爵永康侯。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was appointed Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: After the revolt was suppressed he was appointed palace attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 世祖南討，以拔為都將，從駕臨江而還。

translations.literal: On Emperor Taiwu's southern campaign, Ba was made chief commander, followed the imperial procession to the Yangzi, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Taiwu's southern campaign, Ba served as chief commander, accompanied the emperor to the Yangzi, and then returned.

sentences.zh: 又共陸真討反氐仇傉檀、強免生，平之。

translations.literal: He also joined Lu Zhen in suppressing the rebellious Di leaders Qiu Zhongtan and Qiang Miansheng and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Lu Zhen in suppressing the Di rebels Qiu Zhongtan and Qiang Miansheng and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 皇興三年，除散騎常侍，尚西河長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangxing he was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, married the Eldest Princess of Xihe, and was made Commandant of Cavalry for the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangxing he was appointed regular attendant of scattered cavalry, married the Eldest Princess of Xihe, and was made commandant of cavalry for the imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 其年，拔族叔劉彧徐州刺史安都據城歸順，敕拔詣彭城勞迎。

translations.literal: That same year, when Ba's clansman by marriage Liu Yu was on the throne and Xu Zhou Inspector Andu held the city and submitted, the emperor ordered Ba to go to Pengcheng to welcome and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, when Emperor Ming of Song held the throne and Xu Province inspector Andu surrendered the city, the emperor ordered Ba to go to Pengcheng to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 除冠軍將軍、南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Champions and Inspector of South Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Establishes Champions and Inspector of South Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 延興二年，除鎮西大將軍、開府，進爵平陽公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanxing he was appointed Grand General Who Pacifies the West with an open office and advanced to Duke of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanxing he was appointed grand general who pacifies the west with an open office and was advanced to Duke of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 三年，拔與南兗州刺史游明根、[2]南陽平太守許含等以治民著稱，徵詣京師。

translations.literal: In the third year, Ba, together with South Yan Province Inspector You Minggen, Nanyangping Administrator Xu Han, and others, was famed for governing the people well and was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Ba, together with South Yan Province inspector You Minggen, Administrator of Nanyangping Xu Han, and others, was summoned to the capital for distinguished civil administration.

sentences.zh: 顯祖親自勞勉，復令還州。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu personally comforted and encouraged them, then sent them back to their provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu personally received and encouraged them, then sent them back to their posts.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，改爵為河東公。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe his title was changed to Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，詔拔入朝，暴病卒，年五十八，贈左光祿大夫，諡曰康。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year he was ordered to court, but died suddenly of illness, aged fifty-eight; he was posthumously made Left Grand Master of the Palace and given the posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year he was summoned to court but died suddenly of illness at fifty-eight; he was posthumously honored as Left Grand Master of the Palace with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 長子胤，字寧宗，少有父風。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yin, styled Ningzong, in youth showed his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yin, styled Ningzong, showed his father's character from an early age.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，拜中散，襲爵鎮西大將軍、河東公，除懸瓠鎮將。

translations.literal: At manhood he was appointed Palace Attendant, inherited the titles Grand General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Hedong, and was made garrison commander of Xuanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching manhood he was appointed palace attendant, inherited the rank of grand general who pacifies the west and the ducal title of Hedong, and was made garrison commander of Xuanhu.

sentences.zh: 蕭賾遣將寇邊，詔胤為都將，與穆亮等拒於淮上。

translations.literal: Xiao Ze sent generals to raid the frontier; the court ordered Yin as chief commander to join Mu Liang and others in resisting them on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Ze sent generals to raid the frontier, Yin was appointed chief commander to join Mu Liang and others in resisting them along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 尋授持節義陽道都將。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was given the staff of authority as chief commander of the Yiyang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon granted the staff of authority as chief commander of the Yiyang circuit.

sentences.zh: 十四年，文明太后公除，高祖詔諸刺史、鎮將曾經近侍者，皆聽赴闕，胤隨例入朝。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when the public mourning for Empress Dowager Wenming ended, Emperor Xiaowen ordered that all inspectors and garrison commanders who had once served near the throne might come to court; Yin entered the capital according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when the public mourning for Empress Dowager Wenming ended, Emperor Xiaowen permitted inspectors and garrison commanders who had once served at court to attend; Yin came to the capital accordingly.

sentences.zh: 屬開革五等，降公為侯。

translations.literal: At the time of the reform abolishing the five ranks of nobility, he was reduced from duke to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When the five ranks of nobility were reformed, his title was reduced from duke to marquis.

sentences.zh: 十七年，高祖南討，詔趙郡王幹、司空穆亮為西道都將。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, on Emperor Xiaowen's southern campaign, Prince Gan of Zhao Commandery and Minister of Works Mu Liang were ordered as chief commanders of the western route.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, on Emperor Xiaowen's southern campaign, Prince Gan of Zhao Commandery and Minister of Works Mu Liang were appointed chief commanders of the western route.

sentences.zh: 時幹年少，未涉軍旅。

translations.literal: Gan was then young and had no experience in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was still young and had no experience of military command.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃除胤假節、假平南將軍，為幹副軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen therefore appointed Yin with provisional staff and the provisional title General Who Pacifies the South as Gan's second-in-command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen therefore appointed Yin provisional general who pacifies the south with provisional staff of authority to serve as Gan's second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 行達裒父，以蕭賾死，班師。

translations.literal: The army reached Poufu; when Xiao Ze died, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Poufu, but withdrew when Xiao Ze died.

sentences.zh: 又為都將，共討秦州反，敗支酉，生擒斬之。

translations.literal: He again served as chief commander in the joint suppression of the Qin Province rebellion, defeated Zhi You, captured him alive, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as chief commander in suppressing the Qin Province rebellion, defeated Zhi You, captured him alive, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 除立忠將軍、河北太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Loyalty and Administrator of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Establishes Loyalty and Administrator of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 郡帶山河，路多盜賊。

translations.literal: The commandery lay among mountains and rivers, and the roads were thick with bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery lay among mountains and rivers, and bandits were common on its roads.

sentences.zh: 有韓馬兩姓，各二千餘家，恃強憑險，最為狡害，劫掠道路，侵暴鄉閭。

translations.literal: The Han and Ma clans, each numbering more than two thousand households, relied on their strength and rugged terrain; they were the most cunning and harmful, plundering the roads and oppressing the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: The Han and Ma clans, each numbering more than two thousand households, relied on their strength and rugged terrain to plunder travelers and terrorize the countryside.

sentences.zh: 胤至郡之日，即收其姦魁二十餘人，一時戮之。

translations.literal: On the day Yin reached the commandery he seized more than twenty of their ringleaders and executed them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Yin took up his post he seized more than twenty of their ringleaders and executed them all at once.

sentences.zh: 於是羣盜懾氣，郡中清肅。

translations.literal: Thereupon the bandits were cowed and the commandery grew orderly and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were cowed, and the commandery became peaceful and orderly.

sentences.zh: 二十三年秋，遇疾，卒於郡，時年四十四，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-third year he fell ill and died in the commandery, aged forty-four; his posthumous name was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twenty-third year he fell ill and died in office at forty-four, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 子裔，字豫孫，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yi, styled Yusun, inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, styled Yusun, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 性豪爽，盛營園宅，賓客聲伎，以恣嬉遊。

translations.literal: By nature bold and open-handed, he lavishly built gardens and mansions and kept guests, musicians, and entertainers for unrestrained pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and open-handed by nature, he lavished expense on gardens and mansions and kept guests, musicians, and entertainers for unrestrained pleasure.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書左外兵郎、左軍將軍，遷征虜將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: He served as Left Outer Troops Attendant of the Masters of Writing and General of the Left Army, then was promoted to General Who Captures Barbarians and Palace Grandee Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left outer troops attendant in the Masters of Writing and as general of the left army, then was promoted to general who captures barbarians and palace grandee attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Inspector of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Inspector of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平西將軍、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 子孝紳，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoshen inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoshen inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 稍遷前將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General of the Vanguard and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to general of the vanguard and grand master of palace counsel.

sentences.zh: 孝紳立行險薄，坐事為河南尹元世儁所劾，死。

translations.literal: Xiaoshen's conduct was treacherous and shallow; for an offense he was impeached by Henan Intendant Yuan Shijun and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoshen's conduct was treacherous and unscrupulous; impeached for an offense by Henan intendant Yuan Shijun, he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 後贈征西將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 胤弟□，字崇業。

translations.literal: Yin's younger brother [, personal name lost in the received text,], styled Chongye.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's younger brother, whose personal name is lost in the received text, used the style Chongye.

sentences.zh: 廣平王懷郎中令、[3]汝陰太守。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Household of Prince Huai of Guangping and as Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the household of Prince Huai of Guangping and as Administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 子修仁，司空行參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xiuren served as Acting Army Aide to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiuren served as acting army aide to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 修仁弟玄景，陳留太守。

translations.literal: Xiuren's younger brother Xuanjing was Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren's younger brother Xuanjing served as Administrator of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 拔弟洪隆，字菩提。

translations.literal: Ba's younger brother Honglong, styled Puti.
translations.idiomatic: Ba's younger brother Honglong, whose style name was Puti.

sentences.zh: 解褐陽平王國常侍，稍遷河東太守。

translations.literal: Upon entering office he became Regular Attendant in the kingdom of Prince of Yangping and was gradually promoted to Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he became regular attendant in the household of the Prince of Yangping and was later promoted to Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 長子驎駒，好讀書。

translations.literal: His eldest son Linju loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Linju was devoted to study.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，除中書博士。

translations.literal: Recommended as a Promoted Scholar, he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a promoted scholar, he was appointed erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，蕭賾使至，乃詔驎駒兼主客郎以接之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe, when Xiao Ze's envoys arrived, the court ordered Linju to serve concurrently as Master of Guests to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taihe, when envoys from Xiao Ze arrived, the court ordered Linju to serve concurrently as master of guests to receive them.

sentences.zh: 十年秋，遇疾卒，時年三十五。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year he fell ill and died, aged thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the tenth year he fell ill and died at the age of thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈寧朔將軍、河東太守，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Hedong, with the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Hedong, with the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 長子慶之，字慶集，頗以學業聞。

translations.literal: His eldest son Qingzhi, styled Qingji, was well known for scholarly accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Qingzhi, styled Qingji, was well known for scholarly achievement.

sentences.zh: 解褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: Upon entering office he became Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he became court gentleman for regular attendance.

sentences.zh: 領侍御史，遷廷尉丞。

translations.literal: He served concurrently as Attending Censor and was promoted to Aide of the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as attending censor and was promoted to aide in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 廷尉寺隣接北城，曾夏日於寺傍執得一狐。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice compound adjoined the northern city wall; one summer a fox was caught beside the compound.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice compound adjoined the northern city wall; one summer a fox was caught beside the offices.

sentences.zh: 慶之與廷尉正博陵崔纂，或以城狐狡害，宜速殺之，或以長育之月，宜待秋分。

translations.literal: Qingzhi and the Director of the Ministry of Justice, Cui Zuan of Boling, debated: some held that a city fox was a cunning menace and should be killed at once, others that in the month when creatures are growing one should wait until the autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi and the ministry director, Cui Zuan of Boling, debated whether the fox, as a cunning creature of the city, should be killed at once or whether, in the season of growth, they should wait until the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 二卿裴廷儁、袁翻互有同異。

translations.literal: The two senior officials Pei Tingjun and Yuan Fan likewise took differing sides.
translations.idiomatic: The senior officials Pei Tingjun and Yuan Fan likewise took opposing views.

sentences.zh: 雖曰戲謔，詞義可觀，事傳於世。

translations.literal: Though offered in jest, the words were worth reading, and the story passed into common talk.
translations.idiomatic: Though offered in jest, their exchange was well turned enough to become widely known.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書郎、兼尚書左丞，為并肆行臺，賜爵龍丘子，行并州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Master of Writing Attendant and served concurrently as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing; he headed the Bing-Si Branch Office, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Longqiu, and acted for the affairs of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to master of writing attendant and served concurrently as left assistant director of the Masters of Writing; he headed the Bing-Si branch office, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Longqiu, and administered Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍、滄州刺史，為葛榮攻圍，城陷。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Cang Province; Ge Rong besieged him and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to general who captures barbarians and Inspector of Cang Province, he was besieged by Ge Rong and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 尋患卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 後贈右將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously made General of the Right and Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously honored as General of the Right and Inspector of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 慶之弟英集，性通率。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's younger brother Yingji was by nature frank and unceremonious.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi's younger brother Yingji was frank and unceremonious by nature.

sentences.zh: 隨舅李崇在揚州積年，以軍功歷司徒鎧曹參軍，稍遷治書侍御史、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He followed his maternal uncle Li Chong for many years in Yang Province; for military merit he rose through the post of Army Aide for Armor in the Ministry of Education and was gradually promoted to Attending Imperial Censor and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry with Unimpeded Access.
translations.idiomatic: He spent many years in Yang Province with his maternal uncle Li Chong; for military merit he rose to army aide for armor under the Minister of Education and was gradually promoted to attending imperial censor and regular attendant of scattered cavalry with unimpeded access.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 驎駒弟鳳子。

translations.literal: Linju's younger brother Fengzi.
translations.idiomatic: Linju's younger brother Fengzi.

sentences.zh: 自徙都洛邑，鳳子兄弟移屬華州河西郡焉。

translations.literal: After the capital was moved to Luoyang, Fengzi and his brothers were transferred to the register of Hexi Commandery in Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was moved to Luoyang, Fengzi and his brothers were registered in Hexi Commandery of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，為太子詹事丞、本州中正。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he served as Aide to the Household of the Heir Apparent and as Rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe he served as aide to the household of the heir apparent and as rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 世宗登阼，轉太尉府鎧曹參軍，稍遷治書侍御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Army Aide for Armor in the Grand Marshal's office and was gradually promoted to Attending Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was transferred to army aide for armor in the Grand Marshal's office and was gradually promoted to attending imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 正始初，為持節、征義陽軍司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he served with the staff of authority as military commissioner for the campaign against Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengshi era he served with the staff of authority as military commissioner for the campaign against Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 還京，其年秋卒，時年四十九，贈陵江將軍、光城太守。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital and died that autumn, aged forty-nine; he was posthumously made General of Lingjiang and Administrator of Guangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital and died that autumn at forty-nine, posthumously honored as General of Lingjiang and Administrator of Guangcheng.

sentences.zh: 鳳子弟驥奴，州主簿。

translations.literal: Fengzi's younger clansman Jinu served as provincial registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Fengzi's younger kinsman Jinu served as provincial registrar.

sentences.zh: 洪隆弟破胡，州治中別駕。

translations.literal: Honglong's younger brother Pohu served as provincial director and vice administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Honglong's younger brother Pohu served as provincial director and vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 稍遷河東太守、征仇池都將。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Administrator of Hedong and chief commander of the campaign against Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Administrator of Hedong and chief commander of the campaign against Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 有六子。

translations.literal: He had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons.

sentences.zh: 長子聰，字延智。

translations.literal: His eldest son Cong, styled Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Cong, whose style name was Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 有世譽。

translations.literal: He enjoyed a reputation that endured for generations.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed a lasting family reputation.

sentences.zh: 累遷治書侍御史、直閣將軍，為高祖所知。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Attending Imperial Censor for Legal Documents and General of the Direct Gate, and came to be known to Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of attending imperial censor for legal documents and general of the direct gate, and came to Emperor Xiaowen's notice.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，除輔國將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was appointed General Who Supports the State and Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he was appointed general who supports the state and Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 卒於州。

translations.literal: He died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈征虜將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as general who captures barbarians and Inspector of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 長子景茂，司州記室從事、猗氏令。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jingmao served as Records Aide in Si Province and as Magistrate of Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jingmao served as records aide in Si Province and as magistrate of Yishi.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 景茂弟孝通，頗有文學。

translations.literal: Jingmao's younger brother Xiaotong was accomplished in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao's younger brother Xiaotong was accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 永安中，中尉高道穆引為御史，歷中書舍人、中書侍郎、常山太守。

translations.literal: During Yong'an, Chief Commandant Gao Daomu brought him in as censor; he served as Secretariat Drafter, Secretariat Attendant, and Administrator of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: During Yong'an, Chief Commandant Gao Daomu recruited him as a censor; he later served as secretariat drafter, secretariat attendant, and Administrator of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 遇惡疾而卒。

translations.literal: He encountered a grave illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He died of a grave illness.

sentences.zh: 聰弟道智，尚書郎。

translations.literal: Cong's younger brother Daozhi was a Master of Writing Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's younger brother Daozhi served as master of writing attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子長瑜，天平中，為征東將軍、洛州刺史，擊賊潼關，沒於陳。

translations.literal: His son Changyu, during Tianping, served as General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Luo Province; attacking bandits at Tong Pass, he was lost in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changyu, during Tianping, served as general who campaigns east and Inspector of Luo Province; attacking bandits at Tong Pass, he was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 贈都督冀定太三州諸軍事、車騎將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Supervisor of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Tai provinces, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as supervisor of military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Tai provinces, general of chariots and cavalry, and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 道智弟仙智，郡功曹。

translations.literal: Daozhi's younger brother Xianzhi served as commandery merit officer.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhi's younger brother Xianzhi served as commandery merit officer.

sentences.zh: 仙智弟曇賢，卒於國子博士。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's younger brother Tanxian died while serving as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's younger brother Tanxian died while serving as erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 小子景淵，尚書左民郎。

translations.literal: His youngest son Jingyuan was Left Populace Attendant of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Jingyuan served as left populace attendant in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 曇賢弟和，字導穆。

translations.literal: Tanxian's younger brother He, styled Daomu.
translations.idiomatic: Tanxian's younger brother He, whose style name was Daomu.

sentences.zh: 解褐大將軍劉昶府行參軍。

translations.literal: Upon entering office he became Acting Army Aide in the household of Grand General Liu Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he became acting army aide in the household of Grand General Liu Chang.

sentences.zh: 轉司空長流參軍，除太尉府主簿，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Long-Service Army Aide under the Minister of Works, appointed Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal's office, and promoted to Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to long-service army aide under the Minister of Works, appointed chief clerk of the Grand Marshal's office, and promoted to grand master of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 永平四年正月，山賊劉龍駒擾亂夏州，詔和發汾、華、東秦、夏四州之眾討龍駒，平之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Yongping, the mountain bandit Liu Longju disturbed Xia Province; He was ordered to raise troops from Fen, Hua, East Qin, and Xia provinces to attack Longju and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of Yongping, the mountain bandit Liu Longju raided Xia Province; He was ordered to raise forces from Fen, Hua, East Qin, and Xia provinces, defeated Longju, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 和因表立東夏州，世宗從之。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized to establish East Xia Province, and Emperor Shizong approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to establish East Xia Province, and Emperor Shizong approved.

sentences.zh: 又行正平、潁川二郡事，除通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He also acted for the affairs of Zhengping and Yingchuan commanderies and was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry with Unimpeded Access.
translations.idiomatic: He also administered Zhengping and Yingchuan commanderies and was appointed regular attendant of scattered cavalry with unimpeded access.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將張齊寇晉壽，詔和兼尚書左丞，為西道行臺，節度都督傅豎眼諸軍，大破齊軍。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent the general Zhang Qi to raid Jinshou; He was ordered to serve concurrently as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, head the western-route branch office, and direct the armies under the supervision of Fu Shuyan, defeating Qi decisively.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan sent Zhang Qi to raid Jinshou, He was ordered to serve concurrently as left assistant director of the Masters of Writing, head the western-route branch office, direct the armies under Fu Shuyan, and inflict a major defeat on the enemy.

sentences.zh: 正光初，除左將軍、南青州刺史，卒於州，年五十五。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengguang he was appointed General of the Left and Inspector of South Qing Province; he died in the province, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengguang he was appointed general of the left and Inspector of South Qing Province; he died in office at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈安北將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as general who pacifies the north and Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 長子元信，武定末，中軍將軍、儀同開府長史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yuanxin, at the end of Wuding, served as General of the Central Army and Chief Clerk of an open office with the insignia of Yitong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yuanxin, at the end of Wuding, served as general of the central army and chief clerk of an open office with yitong insignia.

sentences.zh: 和弟季令，奉朝請。

translations.literal: The younger brother Jiling was a Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother Jiling served as court gentleman for regular attendance.

sentences.zh: 破胡弟破氐，為本州別駕，早卒。

translations.literal: Pohu's younger brother Podi served as vice administrator of his home province and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Pohu's younger brother Podi served as vice administrator of his home province and died young.

sentences.zh: 四子。

translations.literal: He had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons.

sentences.zh: 長子敬賢，為鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jingxian was Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jingxian served as Administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 破氐弟積善，為中書博士、臨淮王提友。

translations.literal: Podi's younger brother Jishan was Erudite of the Secretariat and a companion of Prince Ti of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Podi's younger brother Jishan was erudite of the Secretariat and a companion of Prince Ti of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 子隆宗，太原太守。

translations.literal: His son Longzong was Administrator of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Longzong served as Administrator of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 寇讚，字奉國，上谷人，因難徙馮翊萬年。

translations.literal: Kou Zan, styled Fengguo, was a native of Shanggu; because of hardship his family moved to Wannian in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zan, styled Fengguo, was a native of Shanggu whose family moved to Wannian in Fengyi during troubled times.

sentences.zh: 父脩之，字延期，苻堅東萊太守。

translations.literal: His father Xiuzhi, styled Yanqi, was Administrator of Donglai under Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiuzhi, styled Yanqi, had been Administrator of Donglai under Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 讚弟謙之有道術，世祖敬重之，故追贈脩之安西將軍、秦州刺史、馮翊公，賜命服，諡曰哀公，詔秦雍二州為立碑於墓。

translations.literal: Zan's younger brother Qianzhi possessed the Way and its arts, and Emperor Taiwu held him in esteem; therefore Xiuzhi was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Fengyi, granted court robes of rank, and given the posthumous name Duke Ai, with orders that Qin and Yong provinces erect a stele at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's younger brother Qianzhi was skilled in Daoist arts and highly regarded by Emperor Taiwu; Xiuzhi was therefore posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Fengyi, granted robes of rank, given the posthumous title Duke Ai, and ordered to receive a tomb stele erected by Qin and Yong provinces.

sentences.zh: 又贈脩之母為馮翊夫人。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's mother was also posthumously made Lady of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's mother was also posthumously honored as Lady of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 及宗從追贈太守、縣令、侯、子、男者十六人，其臨民者七郡、五縣。

translations.literal: Among his clansmen and followers, sixteen persons were posthumously awarded the ranks of administrator, magistrate, marquis, viscount, and baron; of those who had governed the people, there were seven commanderies and five counties.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen kinsmen and followers were posthumously granted ranks from administrator and magistrate down to marquis, viscount, and baron; those who had governed the people had held seven commanderies and five counties.

sentences.zh: 讚少以清素知名，身長八尺，姿容嚴嶷，非禮不動。

translations.literal: Zan was known from youth for purity and simplicity; eight feet tall, with a stern and imposing bearing, he would not stir except by ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was known from youth for purity and restraint; eight feet tall, stern and imposing in bearing, he would not act except in accordance with propriety.

sentences.zh: 苻堅僕射韋華，州里高達，雖年時有異，恒以風味相待。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's Vice Director Wei Hua was an eminent man of the province; though their ages differed, he always treated Zan with genuine regard.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hua, vice director under Fu Jian, was a leading figure of the region; though they were of different generations, he always treated Zan with genuine esteem.

sentences.zh: 華為馮翊太守，召為功曹，後除襄邑令。

translations.literal: When Hua became Administrator of Fengyi, he summoned Zan as merit officer; later Zan was appointed Magistrate of Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua became Administrator of Fengyi, he summoned Zan as merit officer; Zan was later appointed magistrate of Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 姚泓滅，秦雍人千有餘家推讚為主，歸順。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed, more than a thousand households of Qin and Yong submitted to Zan as their leader and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Yao Hong, more than a thousand households from Qin and Yong chose Zan as their leader and submitted to Wei.

sentences.zh: 拜綏遠將軍、魏郡太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who pacifies the distant and Administrator of Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其後，秦雍之民來奔河南、滎陽、河內者戶至萬數，拜讚安遠將軍、南雍州刺史、軹縣侯，治于洛陽，立雍州之郡縣以撫之。

translations.literal: Afterward, households of Qin and Yong who fled to Henan, Xingyang, and Henei numbered in the tens of thousands; Zan was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant, Inspector of South Yong Province, and Marquis of Zhixian, with his seat at Luoyang, where Yong Province commanderies and counties were established to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward tens of thousands of households from Qin and Yong fled to Henan, Xingyang, and Henei; Zan was appointed general who pacifies the distant, Inspector of South Yong Province, and Marquis of Zhixian, with his seat at Luoyang, where commanderies and counties of Yong Province were established to settle them.

sentences.zh: 由是流民繈負自遠而至，參倍於前。

translations.literal: Thereupon displaced people came from afar carrying their children on their backs, more than triple the number before.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced families then came from far away carrying children on their backs, more than triple the number before.

sentences.zh: 賜讚爵河南公，加安南將軍，領護南蠻校尉，仍刺史，分洛豫二州之僑郡以益之。

translations.literal: Zan was enfeoffed as Duke of Henan, given the additional title General Who Pacifies the South, made Colonel Protecting the Southern Man while retaining his inspectorship, and allotted refugee commanderies from Luo and Yu provinces to enlarge his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Henan, promoted to general who pacifies the south, made colonel protecting the southern Man while remaining inspector, and given refugee commanderies from Luo and Yu provinces to enlarge his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 雖位高爵重而接待不倦。

translations.literal: Though his rank was high and his enfeoffment weighty, he never wearied in receiving people.
translations.idiomatic: Though his rank and title were exalted, he never wearied in receiving those who came to him.

sentences.zh: 初，讚之未貴也，嘗從相者唐文相，文曰：「君額上黑子入幘，位當至方伯封公。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Zan had risen to eminence, he once had his physiognomy read by Tang Wen, who said, "The black mole on your forehead lies within the line of the cap; your position will reach regional lord and enfeoffment as duke."
translations.idiomatic: Before Zan had risen to eminence, he once consulted the physiognomist Tang Wen, who said, "The black mole on your forehead lies within the line of the cap; you will rise to regional lord and be enfeoffed as duke."

sentences.zh: 」及貴也，文以民禮拜謁，仍曰：「明公憶民疇昔之言乎？

translations.literal: When Zan had become eminent, Wen came to pay his respects with the courtesy due a commoner and said, "Does my lord recall what this commoner once said?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zan had become eminent, Wen came to pay his respects as a commoner and said, "Does my lord recall what I once told you?"

sentences.zh: 爾日但知公當貴，然不能自知得為州民也。

translations.literal: That day I knew only that you would become eminent, yet I could not know that I myself would become a subject of your province.
translations.idiomatic: That day I knew only that you would rise, yet I could not have known that I myself would become one of your subjects.

sentences.zh: 」讚曰：「往時卿言杜瓊不得官長，人咸謂不然。

translations.literal: Zan said, "In former days you said Du Qiong would not obtain a post as chief official; everyone said you were wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Zan said, "In former days you said Du Qiong would never obtain a chief official post; everyone said you were wrong."

sentences.zh: 及瓊被選為盩厔令，卿猶言相中不見，而瓊果以暴疾，未拜而終。

translations.literal: When Qiong was selected as Magistrate of Zhouzhi, you still said the physiognomy did not show it, yet Qiong indeed died suddenly of illness before assuming the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiong was selected as magistrate of Zhouzhi, you still said his physiognomy did not show it, yet Qiong died suddenly of illness before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 昔魏舒見主人兒死，自知己必至公，吾常以卿言瓊之驗，亦復不息此望也。

translations.literal: In old times Wei Shu, seeing his master's son die, knew he himself would reach the rank of duke; I have always taken your words about Qiong as proof, and I have never ceased to cherish this hope.
translations.idiomatic: In old times Wei Shu, seeing his master's son die, knew he himself would reach high office; I have always taken your words about Qiong as proof, and I have never ceased to hope for the same.

sentences.zh: 」乃賜文衣服、良馬。

translations.literal: He then bestowed on Wen robes and a fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: He then bestowed robes and a fine horse on Wen.

sentences.zh: 讚在州十七年，甚獲公私之譽，年老表求致仕。

translations.literal: Zan served in the province for seventeen years and won great praise in public and private affairs; in old age he memorialized requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Zan governed the province for seventeen years with great public and private acclaim; in old age he memorialized requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 真君九年卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth year of Zhenjun, aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Zhenjun at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 遺令薄葬，斂以時服。

translations.literal: His final instructions ordered a simple burial and interment in the garments of his time.
translations.idiomatic: His final instructions called for a simple burial in everyday garments.

sentences.zh: 世祖悼惜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu mourned and regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 諡曰宣穆。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Xuanmu.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Xuanmu.

sentences.zh: 長子元寶，襲爵，為豫州別駕。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yuanbao inherited the enfeoffment and served as vice administrator of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yuanbao inherited the title and served as vice administrator of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 與安元年卒，贈安南將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yuan'an and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Yuan'an and was posthumously honored as general who pacifies the south and Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 子祖，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zu inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: [4]高祖時，為安南將軍、東徐州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he served as General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of East Xu Province, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he served as general who pacifies the south and Inspector of East Xu Province, then died.

sentences.zh: 子靈孫，襲。

translations.literal: His son Lingsun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingsun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 赭陽太守。

translations.literal: He was Administrator of Zheyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Zheyang.

sentences.zh: 元寶弟虎皮，有才器。

translations.literal: Yuanbao's younger brother Hupi had talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao's younger brother Hupi was talented and capable.

sentences.zh: 本縣令。

translations.literal: He was magistrate of his home county.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of his home county.

sentences.zh: 虎皮弟臻，字仙勝。

translations.literal: Hupi's younger brother Zhen, styled Xiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hupi's younger brother Zhen, whose style name was Xiansheng.

sentences.zh: 年十二，遭父憂，居喪以孝稱。

translations.literal: At twelve he suffered his father's death and was famed for filial mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he lost his father and was famed for filial observance of mourning.

sentences.zh: 輕財好士。

translations.literal: He treated wealth lightly and delighted in supporting gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He treated wealth lightly and delighted in supporting men of worth.

sentences.zh: 顯祖末，為中川太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xianzu's reign he was Administrator of Zhongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xianzu's reign he served as Administrator of Zhongchuan.

sentences.zh: 時馮熙為洛州刺史，政號貪虐。

translations.literal: At that time Feng Xi was Inspector of Luo Province, and his rule was called greedy and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Feng Xi was Inspector of Luo Province, notorious for greedy and cruel government.

sentences.zh: 仙勝微能附之，甚得其意。

translations.literal: Xiansheng was able in small ways to attach himself to Feng and won his strong approval.
translations.idiomatic: Xiansheng managed to attach himself to Feng and won his strong favor.

sentences.zh: 轉弘農太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrator of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 後以母老屢求解任，久乃從之。

translations.literal: Later, because his mother was old, he repeatedly requested release from office, and only after a long time was his request granted.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because his mother was old, he repeatedly asked to resign, and only after a long delay was his request granted.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，母憂未闋，以恒農大盜張煩等賊害良善，徵為都將，與荊州刺史公孫初頭等追揃之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, before his mourning period had ended, because the great bandits of Hengnong, Zhang Fan and others, preyed on the good, he was summoned as chief commander to pursue and suppress them together with Jing Province Inspector Gongsun Chutou and others.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, before his mourning period had ended, he was summoned as chief commander to pursue the great Hengnong bandits Zhang Fan and others, who preyed on the innocent, together with Jing Province inspector Gongsun Chutou and others.

sentences.zh: 拜振武將軍、比陽鎮將，[5]有威惠之稱。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Inspires Martial Awe and garrison commander of Biyang, and was known for combining authority with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who inspires martial awe and garrison commander of Biyang, and was known for combining stern authority with kindness.

sentences.zh: 遷建威將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who establishes might and Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 及高祖南遷，郢州地為王畿，除弘農太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital south, Ying Province's territory became part of the metropolitan region, and Zhen was appointed Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital south and Ying Province became part of the metropolitan region, Zhen was appointed Administrator of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 坐受納，為御史所彈，遂廢卒於家。

translations.literal: For accepting bribes he was impeached by the censorate, dismissed, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached by the censorate for accepting bribes, he was dismissed and died at home.

sentences.zh: 長子祖訓，順陽太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zuxun was Administrator of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zuxun served as Administrator of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 祖訓弟治，字祖禮。

translations.literal: Zuxun's younger brother Zhi, styled Zuli.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxun's younger brother Zhi, whose style name was Zuli.

sentences.zh: 自洛陽令稍遷鎮遠將軍、東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: From Magistrate of Luoyang he was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of East Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Luoyang he was gradually promoted to general who pacifies the distant and Inspector of East Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 代下之後，蠻民以刺史酈道元峻刻，請治為刺史。

translations.literal: After he came down from the north, the tribal peoples, finding Inspector Li Daoyuan harsh and exacting, requested that Zhi be made inspector.
translations.idiomatic: After his arrival from the north, the tribal peoples, finding Inspector Li Daoyuan harsh and exacting, petitioned to have Zhi appointed inspector in his place.

sentences.zh: 朝議以邊民宜悅，乃以治代道元，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: The court judged that frontier peoples should be pleased, and so Zhi replaced Daoyuan and was advanced to General Who Captures Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged that frontier peoples should be appeased, and so Zhi replaced Daoyuan and was promoted to general who captures barbarians.

sentences.zh: 坐遣戍兵送道元，免官。

translations.literal: For dispatching garrison troops to escort Daoyuan, he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: For dispatching garrison troops to escort Daoyuan out of the province, he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 治兄弟並孝友敦穆，白首同居。

translations.literal: Zhi and his brothers were all filial, friendly, and harmonious, dwelling together until their hair turned white.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and his brothers were all filial, friendly, and harmonious, living together until old age.

sentences.zh: 父亡雖久，而猶於平生所處堂宇，備設幃帳几杖，以時節開堂列拜，垂淚陳薦，若宗廟然，吉凶之事必先啟告，遠出行反亦如之。

translations.literal: Though their father had long been dead, they still furnished the hall where he had lived in life with curtains, canopies, tables, and staffs; at the proper seasons they opened the hall, lined up to bow, and with tears offered sacrifices as if at an ancestral temple. For matters fortunate or ill they always reported first to him, and when traveling far or returning they did the same.
translations.idiomatic: Though their father had long been dead, they still furnished his former hall with curtains, canopies, tables, and staffs; at the proper seasons they opened the hall, bowed in order, and with tears made offerings as at an ancestral temple. For good or ill fortune they always reported to him first, and they did the same when leaving on a distant journey or returning.

sentences.zh: 治，世宗末，遷前將軍、河州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhi, at the end of Emperor Shizong's reign, was promoted to General of the Vanguard and Inspector of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Shizong's reign, Zhi was promoted to general of the vanguard and Inspector of He Province.

sentences.zh: 在任數年，遇却鐵怱反，又為城民詣都列其貪狀十六條。

translations.literal: After several years in office he encountered the rebellion of Qietiecong, and the people of the city also went to the capital to list sixteen counts of his greed.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he faced the rebellion of Qietiecong, and the city's residents also went to the capital to lodge sixteen charges of corruption against him.

sentences.zh: 會赦免。

translations.literal: He was spared when an amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared when an amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 久之，兼廷尉卿，又兼尚書。

translations.literal: After a long time he served concurrently as Director of the Ministry of Justice and again concurrently in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he served concurrently as director of the Ministry of Justice and again concurrently in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 畏避勢家，承顏候色，不能有所執據。

translations.literal: He feared and avoided powerful families, accommodating their expressions and watching their moods, and could not hold to any firm position.
translations.idiomatic: He feared powerful families, deferred to their moods, and could not hold to any firm position.

sentences.zh: 尋遷金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to grand master of the palace with the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 是時，蠻反於三鵶，治為都督追討，戰沒。

translations.literal: At that time the tribes rebelled at Sanyu; Zhi served as supervisor in pursuit and was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the tribes rebelled at Sanyu; Zhi led the pursuit as supervisor and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈持節、都督雍華岐三州諸軍事、衞大將軍、七兵尚書、雍州刺史、昌平男。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the staff of authority, made Supervisor of all military affairs in Yong, Hua, and Qi provinces, Grand General of the Guard, Minister of the Seven Troops, Inspector of Yong Province, and Baron of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the staff of authority, made supervisor of military affairs in Yong, Hua, and Qi provinces, grand general of the guard, minister of the seven troops, Inspector of Yong Province, and Baron of Changping.

sentences.zh: 治弟彌，兼尚書郎。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Mi served concurrently as Master of Writing Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Mi served concurrently as master of writing attendant.

sentences.zh: 為城陽王徽所親待。

translations.literal: He was treated with intimacy by Prince Hui of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was treated with intimacy by Prince Hui of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 永安末，徽避尒朱兆脫身南走。

translations.literal: At the end of Yong'an, Hui fled south to escape Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yong'an, Hui fled south to escape Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 歸命於彌。

translations.literal: He placed himself under Mi's protection.
translations.idiomatic: He placed himself under Mi's protection.

sentences.zh: 彌不納，遣人加害，時論深責之。

translations.literal: Mi would not receive him and sent men to kill him; public opinion deeply condemned Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Mi refused him and sent men to kill him; public opinion deeply condemned Mi.

sentences.zh: 後沒關西。

translations.literal: Later he perished in Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He later perished in Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 治長子朏之，字長明。

translations.literal: Zhi's eldest son Feizhi, styled Changming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's eldest son Feizhi, whose style name was Changming.

sentences.zh: 自直後、奉朝請，再遷鎮遠將軍、諫議大夫，仍直後。

translations.literal: From Direct Attendant and Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance he was twice promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distant and Grand Master of Remonstrance, while retaining his post as Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: From direct attendant and court gentleman for regular attendance he was twice promoted to general who pacifies the distant and grand master of remonstrance, while retaining his post as direct attendant.

sentences.zh: 建義中，出除冠軍將軍、東荊州刺史，兼尚書，為荊郢行臺。

translations.literal: During Jianyi he was sent out as General Who Establishes Champions and Inspector of East Jing Province, serving concurrently in the Masters of Writing and heading the Jing-Ying branch office.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianyi he was sent out as general who establishes champions and Inspector of East Jing Province, serving concurrently in the Masters of Writing and heading the Jing-Ying branch office.

sentences.zh: 代遷，[6]除征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When he returned from the north he was appointed General Who Captures Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from the north he was appointed general who captures barbarians.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，襲爵，又為東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: During Putai he inherited the enfeoffment and again became Inspector of East Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Putai he inherited the title and again became Inspector of East Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he was General Who Guards the East and Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was general who guards the east and grand master of the palace with the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 武定四年卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Wuding, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Wuding at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 酈範，字世則，小名記祖，范陽涿鹿人。

translations.literal: Li Fan, styled Shize, with the childhood name Jizu, was a native of Zhuolu in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan, styled Shize, childhood name Jizu, was a native of Zhuolu in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖紹，慕容寶濮陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was Administrator of Puyang under Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao had been Administrator of Puyang under Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 太祖定中山，以郡迎降，授兗州監軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu pacified Zhongshan, Shao surrendered the commandery and was appointed Military Overseer of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu pacified Zhongshan, Shao surrendered the commandery and was appointed military overseer of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 父嵩，天水太守。

translations.literal: His father Song was Administrator of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Song had been Administrator of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 範，世祖時給事東宮。

translations.literal: Fan, during Emperor Taiwu's reign, served in attendance in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taiwu's reign, Fan served in attendance in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 高宗踐阼，追錄先朝舊勳，賜爵永寧男，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he recorded the meritorious service of the former court and enfeoffed Fan as Baron of Yongning, with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he recognized Fan's family's earlier service and enfeoffed him as Baron of Yongning with the additional rank of general who pacifies the distant.

sentences.zh: 以治禮郎奉遷世祖、恭宗神主於太廟，進爵為子。

translations.literal: As Master of Rites Attendant he escorted the spirit tablets of Emperor Shizu and Emperor Gongzong to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was advanced to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: As master of rites attendant he escorted the spirit tablets of Emperors Shizu and Gongzong to the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was advanced to viscount.

sentences.zh: 征南大將軍慕容白曜南征，範為左司馬。

translations.literal: When Grand General Who Campaigns South Murong Baiyao campaigned south, Fan served as Left Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Who Campaigns South Murong Baiyao campaigned south, Fan served as left chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 師次無鹽，劉彧戍主申纂憑城拒守。

translations.literal: The army halted at Wuyan, where Liu Yu's garrison commander Shen Zuan held the city and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Wuyan, where Liu Yu's garrison commander Shen Zuan held the city and resisted.

sentences.zh: 識者僉以攻具未周，不宜便進。

translations.literal: Those with judgment all agreed that siege equipment was not yet complete and that they should not advance at once.
translations.idiomatic: The advisers all agreed that siege equipment was not yet ready and that they should not advance immediately.

sentences.zh: 範曰：「今輕軍遠襲，深入敵境，無宜淹留，久稽機候。

translations.literal: Fan said: "We now have light forces striking from afar, deep in enemy territory; we ought not linger and long delay the moment of opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Fan said: "We have sent light troops on a distant raid deep into enemy territory; we must not linger and let the moment slip away.

sentences.zh: 且纂必以我軍來速，不去攻守，[7]謂方城可憑，弱卒可恃。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zuan is sure to think our army came quickly and will not abandon defense to attack; he will rely on his walled city and trust in weak troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan will surely think our army arrived in haste and will not leave the walls to fight; he will trust in his fortifications and lean on his weak garrison.

sentences.zh: 此天亡之時也。

translations.literal: This is the hour of Heaven's destruction for him.
translations.idiomatic: This is the hour Heaven has set for his ruin.

sentences.zh: 今若外潛威形，內整戎旅，密厲將士，出其非意，可一攻而克之。

translations.literal: If we now outwardly conceal our martial display and inwardly array our troops, secretly urging the officers and men to strike beyond his expectation, we can take the city in one assault.
translations.idiomatic: If we now hide our strength outwardly while drilling the army within, secretly steeling the officers and men to strike where he does not expect, we can take the city in a single assault.

sentences.zh: 」白曜曰：「一日縱敵，數世之患，今若舒遲，民心固矣。

translations.literal: " Baiyao said: "To let the enemy go for one day is a calamity for generations; if we delay now, the people's hearts will be firm.
translations.idiomatic: " Baiyao said: "To let the enemy slip for one day brings trouble for generations; if we delay now, the people's hearts will harden.

sentences.zh: 司馬之策是也。

translations.literal: The Chief of Staff's plan is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The chief of staff's plan is right.

sentences.zh: 」遂潛軍偽退，示以不攻。

translations.literal: " They then secretly withdrew the army in feigned retreat, showing that they would not attack.
translations.idiomatic: " They then secretly withdrew in a feigned retreat, giving the appearance that they would not attack.

sentences.zh: 纂果不設備，於是即夜部分，旦便騰城，崇朝而克。

translations.literal: Zuan indeed made no preparations; that night they deployed their forces, and at dawn they scaled the walls and took the city by midday.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan indeed made no preparations; that night they deployed their forces, and at dawn they scaled the walls and took the city before noon.

sentences.zh: 白曜將盡以其人為軍實。

translations.literal: Baiyao was about to use all the captives as military assets.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao was about to use all the captives as military assets.

sentences.zh: 範曰：「齊四履之地，世號『東秦』，不遠為經略，恐未可定也。

translations.literal: Fan said: "Qi is a land touching the four seas, known the world over as 'Eastern Qin'; if we do not take a long view in our strategy, I fear we cannot yet secure it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan said: "Qi is a land on all four sides of the sea, known throughout the world as Eastern Qin; without a far-reaching strategy, I fear we cannot yet secure it.

sentences.zh: 今皇威始被，民未霑澤，連城有懷貳之將，比邑有拒守之夫。

translations.literal: Now that imperial majesty has only begun to reach them and the people have not yet received its grace, every linked city has generals with divided loyalties and every neighboring town has men who will resist.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial majesty has only just reached them and the people have not yet felt its grace; in every linked city are generals with divided hearts, and in every neighboring town are men who will hold out.

sentences.zh: [8]宜先信義，示之軌物，然後民心可懷，二州可定。

translations.literal: We should first show faith and righteousness and display our standards to them; only then can the people's hearts be won and the two provinces secured.
translations.idiomatic: We should first show faith and righteousness and teach them our standards; only then can the people's hearts be won and the two provinces secured.

sentences.zh: 」白曜曰：「此良策也。

translations.literal: " Baiyao said: "This is an excellent plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Baiyao said: "This is an excellent plan.

sentences.zh: 」乃免之。

translations.literal: " He then spared them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then spared them.

sentences.zh: 進次肥城，白曜將攻之。

translations.literal: The army advanced to Feicheng; Baiyao was about to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced to Feicheng, and Baiyao was about to attack it.

sentences.zh: 範曰：「肥城雖小，攻則淹日，得之無益軍聲，失之有損威勢。

translations.literal: Fan said: "Feicheng is small, but an assault would cost days; to take it would not enhance our army's renown, while failure would damage our prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Fan said: "Feicheng is small, but an assault would cost days; taking it would not enhance our army's renown, while failure would damage our prestige.

sentences.zh: 且見無鹽之卒，死者塗炭，成敗之機，足為鑒矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, you have seen the troops at Wuyan—dead men heaped like charcoal; the lesson of success and failure is warning enough.
translations.idiomatic: You have already seen the men at Wuyan—dead piled like charcoal; the turning point between success and failure is warning enough.

sentences.zh: 若飛書告喻，可不攻自伏；

translations.literal: If we send flying letters to announce and instruct them, they may submit without fighting;
translations.idiomatic: If we send swift letters to announce and instruct them, they may submit without a fight;

sentences.zh: 縱其不降，亦當逃散。

translations.literal: even if they do not surrender, they should still scatter in flight.
translations.idiomatic: and even if they do not surrender, they should still scatter and flee.

sentences.zh: 」白曜乃以書曉之，肥城果潰。

translations.literal: " Baiyao then sent a letter to enlighten them, and Feicheng indeed collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: " Baiyao then sent a letter to enlighten them, and Feicheng indeed collapsed.

sentences.zh: 白曜目範於眾曰：「此行也，得卿，三齊不足定矣。」

translations.literal: Baiyao looked at Fan before the assembled officers and said: "On this campaign, having gained you, the three Qi regions are not enough to remain undetermined."
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao looked at Fan before the assembled officers and said: "On this campaign, having gained you, the three Qi regions are as good as settled."

sentences.zh: 軍達升城，劉彧太原太守房崇吉棄母妻東走。

translations.literal: The army reached Shengcheng; Liu Yu's Administrator of Taiyuan Fang Chongji abandoned his mother and wife and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Shengcheng; Liu Yu's Administrator of Taiyuan, Fang Chongji, abandoned his mother and wife and fled east.

sentences.zh: 彧青州刺史沈文秀遣其寧朔將軍張元孫奉牋歸款，請軍接援。

translations.literal: Liu Yu's Inspector of Qing Province Shen Wenxiu sent his General Who Pacifies the North Zhang Yuansun with a memorial of submission, requesting that troops be sent to receive and aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's Inspector of Qing Province, Shen Wenxiu, sent his General Who Pacifies the North, Zhang Yuansun, with a memorial of submission, asking that troops be sent to receive and support him.

sentences.zh: 白曜將遣偏師赴之。

translations.literal: Baiyao was about to dispatch a detached force to go there.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao was about to dispatch a detached force to go there.

sentences.zh: 範曰：「桑梓之戀，有懷同德。

translations.literal: Fan said: "Love of one's native land moves all who share the same heart.
translations.idiomatic: Fan said: "Love of one's native land moves all who share the same heart.

sentences.zh: 文秀家在江南，青土無墳栢之累。

translations.literal: Wenxiu's family is in the southland; on Qing soil he has no burden of ancestral graves and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu's family is in the southland; on Qing soil he has no ancestral graves to bind him.

sentences.zh: 擁眾數萬，勁甲堅城，強則拒戰，勢屈則走。

translations.literal: He commands tens of thousands, with strong armor and stout walls; when strong he will resist in battle, and when pressed he will flee.
translations.idiomatic: He commands tens of thousands, with strong armor and stout walls; when strong he will fight, and when pressed he will flee.

sentences.zh: 師未逼之，朝夕無患，竟何所畏，已求援軍？

translations.literal: Our army has not yet forced him; day and night he faces no peril—what could he fear, that he already seeks reinforcements?
translations.idiomatic: Our army has not yet pressed him; day and night he faces no danger—what has he to fear, that he already asks for reinforcements?

sentences.zh: 且觀其使，詞煩而顏愧，視下而志怯，幣厚言甘，誘我也。

translations.literal: Moreover, observe his envoy: his words are many and his face ashamed, he looks down and his will is timid; rich gifts and sweet speech—he is baiting us.
translations.idiomatic: Look at his envoy: his words are many and his face ashamed; he looks down and his spirit is timid—rich gifts and sweet speech. He is baiting us.

sentences.zh: 若不遠圖，懼虧軍勢。

translations.literal: If we do not plan for the distant objective, I fear we will impair our military strength.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not plan for the larger aim, I fear we will weaken our army's position.

sentences.zh: 既進無所取，退逼強敵，羝羊觸蕃，羸角之謂。

translations.literal: Having advanced with nothing to gain and retreating to press a strong foe is like a ram butting a fence—breaking its horns, as the saying goes.
translations.idiomatic: To advance with nothing to gain and retreat only to press a strong foe is like a ram butting a fence—breaking its horns, as the saying goes.

sentences.zh: 未若先守歷城，平盤陽，下梁鄒，克樂陵，然後方軌連鑣，揚旌直進，何患不壺漿路左以迎明公者哉！

translations.literal: Better first to secure Licheng, pacify Panyang, take Liangzou, and capture Leling; then, with chariots aligned and horses hitched abreast, raise the banners and drive straight forward—why worry that the people will not bring rice wine by the roadside to welcome you, my lord!
translations.idiomatic: Better first to secure Licheng, pacify Panyang, take Liangzou, and capture Leling; then, with chariots aligned wheel to wheel and horses abreast, raise the banners and drive straight forward—why worry that the people will not bring rice wine by the roadside to welcome you, my lord!

sentences.zh: 」白曜曰：「卿前後納策，皆不失衷，今日之算，吾所不取。

translations.literal: " Baiyao said: "The plans you have offered before and after have all hit the mark; today's calculation I will not adopt.
translations.idiomatic: " Baiyao said: "The plans you have offered before and after have all been sound; today's calculation I will not accept.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?
