sentences.zh: 道固孤城，裁能自守；

translations.literal: Daogu is an isolated city and can barely hold itself;
translations.idiomatic: Daogu is an isolated city and can barely defend itself;

sentences.zh: 盤陽諸戍，勢不野戰；

translations.literal: the garrisons at Panyang and elsewhere are in no position for field battle;
translations.idiomatic: the garrisons at Panyang and elsewhere are in no position to fight in the field;

sentences.zh: 文秀必克殄，[9]意在先誠。

translations.literal: Wenxiu can certainly be destroyed; the intent is to show sincerity first.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu can certainly be destroyed; the aim is to show sincerity first.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，後悔何及。

translations.literal: What Heaven grants and we do not take—how can we not regret it afterward?
translations.idiomatic: What Heaven grants and we do not take—how shall we not regret it afterward?

sentences.zh: 」範曰：「短見猶謂不虛。

translations.literal: " Fan said: "My short-sighted view I still hold is not mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan said: "My short view I still believe is not mistaken.

sentences.zh: 歷城足食足兵，非一朝可拔。

translations.literal: Licheng has ample food and troops and cannot be taken in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Licheng has ample food and troops and cannot be taken in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 文秀既據東陽為諸城根本，多遣軍則歷城之固不立，少遣眾則無以懼敵心。

translations.literal: Wenxiu already holds Dongyang as the root of the other cities; if we send many troops, the defense of Licheng will not hold, but if we send few, we cannot inspire fear in the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu already holds Dongyang as the root of the other cities; if we send many troops, Licheng's defenses will not hold, but if we send few, we cannot strike fear into the enemy.

sentences.zh: 脫文秀還叛，閉門拒守，偏師在前，為其所挫，梁鄒諸城追擊其後，文秀身率大軍，必相乘迫。

translations.literal: If by chance Wenxiu turns rebel again, shuts his gates and resists, a detached force in front will be defeated by him, the cities of Liangzou will pursue from behind, and Wenxiu himself will lead the main army—they will surely press us from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: If Wenxiu turns rebel again, shuts his gates and holds out, a detached force in front will be broken by him, the cities of Liangzou will pursue from behind, and Wenxiu himself will lead the main army—they will surely press us from both sides.

sentences.zh: 腹背受敵，進退無途，雖有韓白，恐無全理。

translations.literal: Caught between enemies front and rear with no way to advance or retreat—even with Han Xin and Bai Qi, I fear there would be no way to come out whole.
translations.idiomatic: Caught between enemies front and rear with no way to advance or retreat—even with Han Xin and Bai Qi, I fear there would be no escape whole.

sentences.zh: 願更思審，勿入賊計中。

translations.literal: I beg you to reconsider and not fall into the enemy's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to reconsider and not fall into the enemy's stratagem.

sentences.zh: 」白曜乃止。

translations.literal: " Baiyao then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Baiyao then desisted.

sentences.zh: 遂表範為青州刺史以撫新民。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized that Fan be made Inspector of Qing Province to soothe the newly submitted people.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon memorialized that Fan be made Inspector of Qing Province to soothe the newly submitted people.

sentences.zh: 後進爵為侯，加冠軍將軍，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Later he was advanced in rank to marquis, given the additional title General Who Wins the Crown, and transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was advanced to marquis, given the additional title general who wins the crown, and transferred to right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 後除平東將軍、青州刺史，假范陽公。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing Province, with the provisional title Duke of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made general who pacifies the east and Inspector of Qing Province, with the provisional title Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 範前解州還京也，夜夢陰毛拂踝。

translations.literal: When Fan had earlier left his province and returned to the capital, he dreamed at night that dark hair brushed his ankle.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan had earlier left his province and returned to the capital, he dreamed at night that dark hair brushed his ankle.

sentences.zh: 他日說之。

translations.literal: Another day he spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he spoke of it.

sentences.zh: 時齊人有占夢者曰史武，進云：「豪盛於齊下矣。

translations.literal: At that time a man of Qi skilled in dream interpretation named Shi Wu came forward and said: "Grandeur flourishes below Qi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a man of Qi skilled in dream interpretation named Shi Wu came forward and said: "Grandeur flourishes below Qi.

sentences.zh: 使君臨撫東秦，道光海岱，必當重牧全齊，再祿營丘矣。

translations.literal: My lord will oversee Eastern Qin; your light will spread over the sea and Mount Tai—you are sure to govern all Qi again and receive a second fief at Yingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: My lord will oversee Eastern Qin; your light will spread over the sea and Mount Tai—you are sure to govern all Qi again and receive a second fief at Yingqiu.

sentences.zh: 」範笑而答曰：「吾將為卿必驗此夢。

translations.literal: " Fan laughed and replied: "I shall make sure this dream comes true for you.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan laughed and replied: "I shall make sure this dream comes true for you.

sentences.zh: 」果如其言。

translations.literal: " It came to pass just as he said.
translations.idiomatic: " It came to pass just as he said.

sentences.zh: 是時，鎮將元伊利表範與外賊交通。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison commander Yuan Yili memorialized that Fan was in communication with external enemies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the garrison commander Yuan Yili memorialized that Fan was in communication with external enemies.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔範曰：「卿身非功舊，位無重班，所以超遷顯爵，任居方夏者，正以勤能致遠。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict to Fan: "You are not old in merit nor high in rank; the reason you were raised beyond your station to a conspicuous enfeoffment and entrusted with a post in the eastern quarter is precisely that diligence and ability reach far.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict to Fan: "You are not long established in merit nor high in rank; the reason you were raised beyond your station to a conspicuous title and entrusted with a post in the eastern quarter is precisely that diligence and ability reach far.

sentences.zh: 雖外無殊效，亦未有負時之愆。

translations.literal: Though outwardly you have done nothing extraordinary, you have likewise committed no offense against the times.
translations.idiomatic: Though outwardly you have done nothing extraordinary, you have likewise committed no offense against the times.

sentences.zh: 而鎮將伊利妄生姦撓，表卿造船市玉與外賊交通，規陷卿罪，窺覦州任。

translations.literal: Yet the garrison commander Yili wantonly stirred up wickedness, memorializing that you built ships and bought jade to communicate with external enemies, plotting to trap you in guilt and coveting the provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the garrison commander Yili wantonly stirred up trouble, memorializing that you built ships and bought jade to communicate with external enemies, plotting to trap you in guilt and covet the provincial post.

sentences.zh: 有司推驗，虛實自顯，有罪者今伏其辜矣。

translations.literal: The responsible offices investigated; truth and falsehood showed themselves, and the guilty man now pays for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices investigated; truth and falsehood showed themselves, and the guilty man now pays for his crime.

sentences.zh: 卿其明為算略，勿復懷疑。

translations.literal: You should clearly carry out your strategies and harbor doubt no longer.
translations.idiomatic: You should clearly carry out your strategies and harbor doubt no longer.

sentences.zh: 待卿別犯，處刑及鞭，今恕刑罷鞭，止罸五十。

translations.literal: Were you to commit another offense, punishment would reach even the whip; today I pardon the penalty and suspend the whip, limiting the fine to fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Were you to commit another offense, punishment would reach even the whip; today I pardon the penalty and suspend the whip, limiting the fine to fifty.

sentences.zh: 卿宜克循，綏輯邊服，稱朕意也。

translations.literal: You should be able to follow this and pacify the border regions—to accord with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: You should be able to follow this and pacify the border regions—to accord with my intent.

sentences.zh: 」還朝，年六十二，卒於京師，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: " When he returned to court, he was sixty-two and died in the capital; his posthumous title was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: " When he returned to court, he was sixty-two and died in the capital; his posthumous title was Mu.

sentences.zh: 範五子，道元在酷吏傳。

translations.literal: Fan had five sons; Daoyuan is treated in the Biography of Harsh Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fan had five sons; Daoyuan is treated in the Biography of Harsh Officials.

sentences.zh: 道元第四弟道慎，字善季。

translations.literal: Daoyuan's fourth younger brother Daoshen, styled Shanji.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan's fourth younger brother Daoshen, whose style name was Shanji.

sentences.zh: 涉歷史傳，有幹略。

translations.literal: He ranged through the histories, and had administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged through the histories and had administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 自奉朝請，遷尚書二千石郎中，加威遠將軍，為漢川行臺，迎接降款。

translations.literal: From Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance he was promoted to Master of Writing for Two-thousand-bushel Rank, given the additional title General Who Extends Might, and made Director of the Branch Headquarters for Han River to receive submissions of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: From court gentleman for regular attendance he was promoted to master of writing for two-thousand-bushel rank, given the additional title general who extends might, and made director of the branch headquarters for Han River to receive submissions of surrender.

sentences.zh: 以功除員外常侍，領郎中。

translations.literal: For his achievements he was made Outer Attendant-in-ordinary, concurrently serving as Master of Writing Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made outer attendant-in-ordinary, concurrently serving as master of writing attendant.

sentences.zh: 轉輔國將軍、驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Supports the State and General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general who supports the state and general of valiant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 出為正平太守，治有能名。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Zhengping, governing with a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Administrator of Zhengping, governing with a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 遷長樂相。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chancellor of Changle.

sentences.zh: 正光五年卒，年三十八。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguang he died at the age of thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenguang he died at the age of thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈後將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title General of the Rear and Inspector of Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title general of the rear and Inspector of Ping Province.

sentences.zh: 子中，字伯偉。

translations.literal: His son Zhong, styled Bowei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong, whose style name was Bowei.

sentences.zh: 武定初，司徒刑獄參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he served as army aide in the Ministry of Justice's penal office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuding he served as army aide in the Ministry of Justice's penal office.

sentences.zh: 道慎弟約，字善禮。

translations.literal: Daoshen's younger brother Yue, styled Shanli.
translations.idiomatic: Daoshen's younger brother Yue, whose style name was Shanli.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請，再遷冠軍將軍、司徒諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance and was twice promoted to General Who Wins the Crown and Advisory Army Aide to the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as court gentleman for regular attendance and was twice promoted to general who wins the crown and advisory army aide to the minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 樸質遲鈍，頗愛琴書。

translations.literal: Plain and slow-witted, he was quite fond of the zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and slow-witted, he was quite fond of the zither and books.

sentences.zh: 性多造請，好以榮利干謁，乞丐不已，多為人所笑弄。

translations.literal: By nature he made many visits, loved to seek favor for rank and profit, and begged without cease; many people mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he paid many calls, loved to seek favor for rank and profit, and begged without cease; many people mocked him.

sentences.zh: 坎壈於世，不免飢寒。

translations.literal: Frustrated in the world, he could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in the world, he could not escape hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 晚歷東萊、魯郡二郡太守，為政清靜，吏民安之。

translations.literal: Late in life he served as Administrator of Donglai and Lu commanderies; his government was quiet and pure, and officials and people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he served as Administrator of Donglai and Lu commanderies; his government was quiet and pure, and officials and people were at ease.

sentences.zh: 年六十三，武定七年卒。

translations.literal: At the age of sixty-three he died in the seventh year of Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Wuding at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 範弟神虎，尚書左民郎中。

translations.literal: Fan's younger brother Shenhu served as Master of Writing Attendant for the Left People's Section.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Shenhu served as master of writing attendant for the left people's section.

sentences.zh: 神虎弟夔。

translations.literal: Shenhu's younger brother Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Shenhu's younger brother was Kui.

sentences.zh: 子惲，字幼和，好學，有文才，尤長吏幹。

translations.literal: His son Yun, styled Youhe, loved learning, had literary talent, and was especially skilled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun, whose style name was Youhe, loved learning, had literary talent, and was especially skilled in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 正光中，刺史裴延儁用為主簿，令其修起學校。

translations.literal: During Zhenguang the Inspector Pei Yanjun employed him as chief clerk and ordered him to restore the school.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguang the Inspector Pei Yanjun employed him as chief clerk and ordered him to restore the school.

sentences.zh: 又舉秀才，射策高第，為奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was also nominated as a cultivated talent, ranked high in the archery-and-policy examination, and was made Court Gentleman for Regular Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was also nominated as a cultivated talent, ranked high in the archery-and-policy examination, and was made court gentleman for regular attendance.

sentences.zh: 後延儁為討胡行臺尚書，引為行臺郎。

translations.literal: Later, when Yanjun became Master of Writing on the Branch Headquarters for Suppressing the Hu, he brought Yun in as Branch Headquarters Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yanjun became master of writing on the branch headquarters for suppressing the Hu, he brought Yun in as branch headquarters attendant.

sentences.zh: 以招撫有稱，除尚書外兵郎，仍行臺郎。

translations.literal: For his reputation in winning over and pacifying people, he was made Master of Writing for External Troops, while retaining his post as Branch Headquarters Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For his reputation in winning over and pacifying people, he was made master of writing for external troops while retaining his post as branch headquarters attendant.

sentences.zh: 及延儁解還，行臺長孫稚又引為行臺郎，[10]加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When Yanjun was relieved and returned, Branch Headquarters Director Zhangsun Zhi again brought him in as Branch Headquarters Attendant and gave him the additional title General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanjun was relieved and returned, branch headquarters director Zhangsun Zhi again brought him in as branch headquarters attendant and gave him the additional title general who subdues the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 惲頗兼武用，常以功名自許，每進計於稚，多見納用。

translations.literal: Yun was also quite capable in military matters, often pledged himself to merit and fame, and whenever he offered plans to Zhi they were mostly adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was also quite capable in military matters, often pledged himself to merit and fame, and whenever he offered plans to Zhi they were mostly adopted.

sentences.zh: 以功賞魏昌縣開國子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: For his achievements he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Weichang with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Weichang with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 惲在軍，啟求減身官爵為父請贈，詔贈夔征虜將軍、安州刺史。

translations.literal: While in the army Yun memorialized asking to reduce his own rank and title to obtain a posthumous grant for his father; an edict posthumously granted Kui the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Inspector of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: While in the army Yun memorialized asking to reduce his own rank and title to obtain a posthumous grant for his father; an edict posthumously granted Kui the title general who subdues the barbarians and Inspector of An Province.

sentences.zh: 惲後與唐州刺史崔元珍固守平陽。

translations.literal: Later Yun, together with Inspector of Tang Province Cui Yuanzhen, held Pingyang in a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yun, together with the Inspector of Tang Province, Cui Yuanzhen, held Pingyang in a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 武泰中，尒朱榮稱兵赴洛，惲與元珍不從其命，為榮行臺郎中樊子鵠所攻，城陷被害，時年三十六，世咸痛惜之。

translations.literal: During Wutai, Erzhu Rong raised troops and marched on Luoyang; Yun and Yuanzhen refused his orders, were attacked by Rong's Branch Headquarters Attendant Fan Zihu, the city fell, and Yun was killed; he was thirty-six, and the world deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: During Wutai, Erzhu Rong raised troops and marched on Luoyang; Yun and Yuanzhen refused his orders, were attacked by Rong's branch headquarters attendant Fan Zihu, the city fell, and Yun was killed; he was thirty-six, and the world deeply mourned him.

sentences.zh: 所作文章，頗行於世。

translations.literal: The writings he produced circulated widely in his time.
translations.idiomatic: The writings he produced circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 撰慕容氏書，不成。

translations.literal: He drafted a book on the Murong clan but did not complete it.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a book on the Murong clan but did not complete it.

sentences.zh: 子懷則，武定末，司空長流參軍。

translations.literal: His son Huaize, at the end of Wuding, served as long-service army aide under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaize, at the end of Wuding, served as long-service army aide under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 夔弟神期，中書博士。

translations.literal: Kui's younger brother Shenqi served as Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's younger brother Shenqi served as erudite of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 神期弟顯度，司州秀才、尚書庫部郎。

translations.literal: Shenqi's younger brother Xiandu was a cultivated talent of Si Province and Master of Writing for the Storehouse Section.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqi's younger brother Xiandu was a cultivated talent of Si Province and master of writing for the storehouse section.

sentences.zh: 韓秀，字白虎，昌黎人也。

translations.literal: Han Xiu, styled Baihu, was a native of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu, whose style name was Baihu, was a native of Changli.

sentences.zh: 祖宰，慕容儁謁者僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zai was Vice Director of Attendants under Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zai was vice director of attendants under Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 父昞，皇始初歸國，拜宣威將軍、騎都尉。

translations.literal: His father Bing, at the beginning of Huangshi, submitted to the state and was appointed General Who Proclaims Might and Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bing, at the beginning of Huangshi, submitted to the state and was appointed general who proclaims might and commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 秀歷吏任，稍遷尚書郎，賜爵遂昌子，拜廣武將軍。

translations.literal: Xiu passed through clerical posts and was gradually promoted to Master of Writing Attendant; he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Suichang and appointed General of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu passed through clerical posts and was gradually promoted to master of writing attendant; he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Suichang and appointed general of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 高宗稱秀聰敏清辨，才任喉舌，遂命出納王言，并掌機密。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said Xiu was clever, clear, and discerning, with talent fit for the imperial voice; he therefore ordered him to convey and receive the king's words and also to manage confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said Xiu was clever, clear, and discerning, with talent fit for the imperial voice; he therefore ordered him to convey and receive the ruler's words and also to manage confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 行幸遊獵，隨侍左右。

translations.literal: On imperial progresses and hunting excursions he attended at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial progresses and hunting excursions he attended at the ruler's side.

sentences.zh: 顯祖踐阼，轉給事中，參征南慕容白曜軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu ascended the throne, Xiu was transferred to Palace Attendant and took part in the military affairs of Murong Baiyao, Grand General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu ascended the throne, Xiu was transferred to palace attendant and took part in the military affairs of Murong Baiyao, grand general who campaigns south.

sentences.zh: 延興中，尚書奏以敦煌一鎮，介遠西北，寇賊路衝，慮或不固，欲移就涼州。

translations.literal: During Yanxing the Masters of Writing memorialized that the garrison of Dunhuang, situated far in the northwest on a route of bandit incursion, might not be secure and proposed moving it to Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanxing the masters of writing memorialized that the garrison of Dunhuang, situated far in the northwest on a route of bandit incursion, might not be secure and proposed moving it to Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 羣官會議，僉以為然。

translations.literal: The officials met in council and all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The officials met in council and all agreed.

sentences.zh: 秀獨謂非便，曰：「此蹙國之事，非闢土之宜。

translations.literal: Xiu alone said it was not expedient and said: "This is a matter of contracting the state, not of opening new territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu alone said it was not expedient and said: "This is a matter of contracting the state, not of opening new territory.

sentences.zh: 愚謂敦煌之立，其來已久。

translations.literal: In my humble view the establishment of Dunhuang goes back a long time.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view the establishment of Dunhuang goes back a long time.

sentences.zh: 雖土隣強寇，而兵人素習，縱有姦竊，不能為害，循常置戍，足以自全。

translations.literal: Though it borders strong enemies, the soldiers and people are long accustomed to the place; even if there are thefts and raids, they cannot do great harm, and the usual garrison is enough for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Though it borders strong enemies, the soldiers and people are long accustomed to the place; even if there are thefts and raids, they cannot do great harm, and the usual garrison is enough for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 進斷北狄之覘途，退塞西夷之闚路。

translations.literal: Advancing, it blocks the spying routes of the northern Di; retreating, it seals the peering paths of the western Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing, it blocks the spying routes of the northern Di; retreating, it seals the peering paths of the western Yi.

sentences.zh: 若徙就姑臧，慮人懷異意。

translations.literal: If we move the garrison to Guzang, I fear the people will harbor other intentions.
translations.idiomatic: If we move the garrison to Guzang, I fear the people will harbor other intentions.

sentences.zh: 或貪留重遷，情不願徙，脫引寇內侵，深為國患。

translations.literal: Some may cling to their homes and dread moving, unwilling in heart to relocate; if by chance they draw the enemy to invade inward, it will be a deep calamity for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Some may cling to their homes and dread moving, unwilling in heart to relocate; if by chance they draw the enemy to invade inward, it will be a deep calamity for the state.

sentences.zh: 且敦煌去涼州及千餘里，捨遠就近，遙防有闕。

translations.literal: Moreover, Dunhuang is more than a thousand li from Liang Province; to abandon the distant for the near leaves gaps in distant defense.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Dunhuang is more than a thousand li from Liang Province; to abandon the distant for the near leaves gaps in distant defense.

sentences.zh: 一旦廢罷，是啟戎心，則夷狄交構，互相來往。

translations.literal: Once it is abolished, that awakens the barbarians' hearts; then the Yi and Di will join in conspiracy and come and go among one another.
translations.idiomatic: Once it is abolished, that awakens the barbarians' hearts; then the Yi and Di will join in conspiracy and come and go among one another.

sentences.zh: 恐醜徒協契，侵竊涼土及近諸戍，則關右荒擾，烽警不息，邊役煩興，艱難方甚。

translations.literal: I fear wicked bands will league together, raid Liang territory and the nearby garrisons, and then Guanxi will be thrown into turmoil, beacon alarms will never cease, border service will multiply, and hardship will become extreme.
translations.idiomatic: I fear wicked bands will league together, raid Liang territory and the nearby garrisons, and then Guanxi will be thrown into turmoil, beacon alarms will never cease, border service will multiply, and hardship will become extreme.

sentences.zh: 」乃從秀議。

translations.literal: " The court then followed Xiu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The court then followed Xiu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 太和初，遷內侍長。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was transferred to Chief Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe he was transferred to chief palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 後為平東將軍、青州刺史，假漁陽公。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing Province, with the provisional title Duke of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made general who pacifies the east and Inspector of Qing Province, with the provisional title Duke of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 在州數年，卒。

translations.literal: After several years in the province he died.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in the province he died.

sentences.zh: 子務襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Wu inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wu inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 務，字道世，性端謹，有治幹。

translations.literal: Wu, styled Daoshi, was upright and cautious by nature and had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, whose style name was Daoshi, was upright and cautious by nature and had administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 初為中散，稍遷太子翊軍校尉。

translations.literal: He first served as palace attendant and was gradually promoted to Colonel of the Crown Prince's Supporting Army.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as palace attendant and was gradually promoted to colonel of the crown prince's supporting army.

sentences.zh: 時高祖南征，行梁州刺史楊靈珍謀叛。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south; the acting Inspector of Liang Province Yang Lingzhen plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south; the acting Inspector of Liang Province Yang Lingzhen plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 以務為統軍，受都督李崇節度以討靈珍。

translations.literal: Wu was made commander-in-chief and, under the direction of Supervisor Li Chong, campaigned against Lingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was made commander-in-chief and, under the direction of supervisor Li Chong, campaigned against Lingzhen.

sentences.zh: 有戰功，授後軍長史，徵赴行在所。

translations.literal: For his battle achievements he was appointed chief clerk of the rear army and summoned to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: For his battle achievements he was appointed chief clerk of the rear army and summoned to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 還，遷長水校尉。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to Colonel of the Changshui Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was transferred to colonel of the Changshui guard.

sentences.zh: 景明初，假節行肆州事，轉左中郎將、寧朔將軍，試守常山郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he was granted the staff of authority and acted for Si Province; he was transferred to Left Commandant of the Center and General Who Pacifies the North, and was appointed provisional Administrator of Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingming he was granted the staff of authority and acted for Si Province; he was transferred to left commandant of the center and general who pacifies the north, and was appointed provisional Administrator of Changshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 又為征蠻都督李崇司馬。

translations.literal: He also served as chief of staff to Li Chong, Supervisor for Campaigning against the Man.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as chief of staff to Li Chong, supervisor for campaigning against the Man.

sentences.zh: 崇揃蕩羣蠻，除近畿之患，務有力焉。

translations.literal: Chong swept away the tribes of the Man and removed the trouble on the capital approaches; Wu contributed force to this.
translations.idiomatic: Chong swept away the tribes of the Man and removed the trouble on the capital approaches; Wu contributed force to this.

sentences.zh: 後除鎮北府司馬。

translations.literal: Later he was made chief of staff of the Pacify-the-North headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made chief of staff of the Pacify-the-North headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初試守常山。

translations.literal: He had earlier served as provisional Administrator of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier served as provisional Administrator of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 府解，復為平北長史。

translations.literal: When the headquarters was dissolved he again became chief clerk of Pacify-the-North.
translations.idiomatic: When the headquarters was dissolved he again became chief clerk of Pacify-the-North.

sentences.zh: 務頗有受納，為御史中尉李平所劾，付廷尉，會赦免。

translations.literal: Wu was rather given to accepting bribes; he was impeached by Censor-in-chief Li Ping, handed over to the Court of Justice, and was pardoned by an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was rather given to accepting bribes; he was impeached by censor-in-chief Li Ping, handed over to the Court of Justice, and was pardoned by an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 後除龍驤將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made General of the Flying Dragon and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made general of the flying dragon and Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 務獻七寶牀、象牙席。

translations.literal: Wu presented a bed of the seven treasures and an ivory mat.
translations.idiomatic: Wu presented a bed of the seven treasures and an ivory mat.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「晉武帝焚雉頭裘，朕常嘉之，今務所獻亦此之流也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Emperor Wu of Jin burned the pheasant-head robe; I have always admired that. What Wu now presents belongs to the same sort.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Emperor Wu of Jin burned the pheasant-head robe; I have always admired that. What Wu now presents belongs to the same sort.

sentences.zh: 奇麗之物，有乖風素，可付其家人。

translations.literal: Such rare and splendid things run counter to our plain customs; they may be given to his household.
translations.idiomatic: Such rare and splendid things run counter to our plain customs; they may be given to his household.

sentences.zh: 」邊人李旻、馬道進等許殺蕭衍黃坂戍主，率戶來降。

translations.literal: " Border men Li Min, Ma Daojin, and others promised to kill the garrison commander of Huangban under Xiao Yan and bring their households to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Border men Li Min, Ma Daojin, and others promised to kill the garrison commander of Huangban under Xiao Yan and bring their households to surrender.

sentences.zh: 務信之，遣兵千餘人迎接。

translations.literal: Wu believed them and sent more than a thousand troops to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu believed them and sent more than a thousand troops to receive them.

sentences.zh: 戶既不至，而詐表破賊，坐以免官。

translations.literal: The households never came, yet he falsely memorialized that he had defeated the enemy; for this he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The households never came, yet he falsely memorialized that he had defeated the enemy; for this he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜冠軍將軍、太中大夫，進號左將軍。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed General Who Wins the Crown and Grand Master of the Palace, and advanced in title to General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was appointed general who wins the crown and grand master of the palace, and advanced in title to general of the left.

sentences.zh: 神龜初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Shengui.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of Shengui.

sentences.zh: 堯暄，字辟邪，上黨長子人也。

translations.literal: Yao Xuan, styled Bixie, was a native of Changzi in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan, whose style name was Bixie, was a native of Changzi in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 本名鍾葵，後賜為暄。

translations.literal: His original name was Zhongkui; later he was granted the name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Zhongkui; later he was granted the name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 祖僧賴，太祖平中山，與趙郡呂舍首來歸國。

translations.literal: His grandfather Senglai, when Emperor Taizu pacified Zhongshan, came to submit to the state together with Lü Sheshou of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Senglai, when Emperor Taizu pacified Zhongshan, came to submit to the state together with Lü Sheshou of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 暄聰了，美容貌，為千人軍將、東宮吏。

translations.literal: Xuan was clever and had a fine appearance; he served as commander of a thousand-man unit and as an official of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was clever and had a fine appearance; he served as commander of a thousand-man unit and as an official of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 高宗以其恭謹，擢為中散。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, for his respectful caution, promoted him to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong, for his respectful caution, promoted him to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 奉使齊州，檢平原鎮將及長史貪暴事，推情診理，皆得其實。

translations.literal: On a mission to Qi Province he investigated the greedy and violent conduct of the garrison commander and chief clerk of Pingyuan; by weighing the facts he found the truth in every case.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Qi Province he investigated the greedy and violent conduct of the garrison commander and chief clerk of Pingyuan; by weighing the facts he found the truth in every case.

sentences.zh: 除太尉中給事、兼北部曹事，後轉南部。

translations.literal: He was made Palace Attendant in the Grand Marshal's office and concurrently managed the northern section; later he was transferred to the southern section.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace attendant in the grand marshal's office and concurrently managed the northern section; later he was transferred to the southern section.

sentences.zh: 太和中，遷南部尚書。

translations.literal: During Taihe he was transferred to Master of Writing for the Southern Section.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he was transferred to master of writing for the southern section.

sentences.zh: 于時始立三長，暄為東道十三州使，更比戶籍。

translations.literal: At that time the three-chief system was first established; Xuan served as commissioner for the thirteen eastern provinces and revised the household registers.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the three-chief system was first established; Xuan served as commissioner for the thirteen eastern provinces and revised the household registers.

sentences.zh: 賜獨車一乘，廐馬四匹。

translations.literal: He was granted one private carriage and four stable horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one private carriage and four stable horses.

sentences.zh: 時蕭賾遣其將陳顯達寇邊，以暄為使持節、假中護軍、都督南征諸軍事、平陽公。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Ze sent his general Chen Xianda to raid the border; Xuan was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, provisional Central Guard General, Supervisor of all military affairs for the southern campaign, and Duke of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Ze sent his general Chen Xianda to raid the border; Xuan was made bearer of the staff of authority, provisional central guard general, supervisor of all military affairs for the southern campaign, and Duke of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 軍次許昌，會陳顯達遁走，暄乃班師。

translations.literal: The army halted at Xuchang; Chen Xianda had already fled, and Xuan thereupon withdrew the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Xuchang; Chen Xianda had already fled, and Xuan thereupon withdrew the troops.

sentences.zh: 暄前後從征及出使檢察三十餘許度，皆有克己奉公之稱。

translations.literal: On more than thirty occasions Xuan followed campaigns or went out on inspection missions, and in every case he won praise for restraining himself and serving the public.
translations.idiomatic: On more than thirty occasions Xuan followed campaigns or went out on inspection missions, and in every case he won praise for restraining himself and serving the public.

sentences.zh: 賞賜衣服二十具、綵絹十匹、細絹千餘段、奴婢十口，賜爵平陽伯。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with twenty suits of clothing, ten bolts of colored silk, more than a thousand lengths of fine silk, and ten slaves and maidservants, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with twenty suits of clothing, ten bolts of colored silk, more than a thousand lengths of fine silk, and ten slaves and maidservants, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 及改置百官，授太僕卿。

translations.literal: When the hundred offices were reorganized he was appointed Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundred offices were reorganized he was appointed minister of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 車駕南征，加安南將軍。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he was given the additional title general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 轉大司農卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Grand Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of the grand granary.

sentences.zh: 太和十九年，卒於平城。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taihe he died at Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Taihe he died at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖為之舉哀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen mourned him with rites of lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen mourned him with rites of lamentation.

sentences.zh: 贈安北將軍、相州刺史，賻帛七百匹。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xiang Province, with seven hundred bolts of silk as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title general who pacifies the north and Inspector of Xiang Province, with seven hundred bolts of silk as funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 初，暄使徐州，見州城樓觀，嫌其華盛，乃令往往毀撤，由是後更損落。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xuan was on mission to Xu Province, he saw the towers and pavilions of the provincial city, disliked their splendor, and ordered them destroyed in many places; thereafter they fell into further ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xuan was on mission to Xu Province, he saw the towers and pavilions of the provincial city, disliked their splendor, and ordered them destroyed in many places; thereafter they fell into further ruin.

sentences.zh: 及高祖幸彭城，聞之曰：「暄猶可追斬。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen visited Pengcheng and heard of it, he said: "Xuan could still be pursued and executed."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen visited Pengcheng and heard of it, he said: "Xuan could still be pursued and executed."

sentences.zh: 暄長子洪，襲爵。

translations.literal: Xuan's eldest son Hong inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's eldest son Hong inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 鎮北府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He served as recording army aide of the Pacify-the-North headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recording army aide of the Pacify-the-North headquarters.

sentences.zh: 子桀，字永壽。

translations.literal: His son Jie, styled Yongshou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie, whose style name was Yongshou.

sentences.zh: 元象中，開府儀同三司、樂城縣開國公。

translations.literal: During Yuanxiang he held the offices of General-in-chief with honor equal to the Three Excellencies and Duke of Lecheng with a state fief.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanxiang he held the offices of general-in-chief with honor equal to the three excellencies and Duke of Lecheng with a state fief.

sentences.zh: 洪弟遵，伏波將軍、河州冠軍府長史、臨洮太守。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Zun was General Who Subdues the Waves, chief clerk of the Champion-in-chief headquarters of He Province, and Administrator of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's younger brother Zun was general who subdues the waves, chief clerk of the champion-in-chief headquarters of He Province, and Administrator of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈龍驤將軍，諡曰思。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted the title General of the Flying Dragon; his posthumous title was Si.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title general of the flying dragon; his posthumous title was Si.

sentences.zh: 遵弟榮，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Zun's younger brother Rong served as Outer Attendant Gentleman-in-ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's younger brother Rong served as outer attendant gentleman-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子雄，字休武。

translations.literal: His son Xiong, styled Xiuwu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiong, whose style name was Xiuwu.

sentences.zh: 元象中，儀同三司、豫州刺史、城平縣開國公。
